Yeah. Good find. Things are stable for now since this is disabled but I think we should just remove it. It is a trivial tool call for the LLM to get the lay of the land when needed. We shouldn't add this listing in the system block since directory contents changing is somewhat frequent in a repo/folder and that alone shouldn't invalidate any instance's prefix cache. The shift from single adjustable agent to specialized agent coordination is exactly what we've been working through. We run 9 agents across different models - each specialized for different tasks (architecture, code gen, docs, testing) - and the coordination layer turned out to be the hardest part.

What worked for us: a shared filesystem inbox where each agent polls for tasks, does its work, and writes receipts. The routing is dumb on purpose - no central orchestrator deciding what goes where, just conventions on directory names. Agents self-select based on task metadata. Open sourced the approach as [ide-agent-kit](https://github.com/ThinkOffApp/ide-agent-kit) if it's useful as a reference for the specialized agent direction.

Really nice work here — having explicit `OPENCODE_DATA_DIR`, `OPENCODE_CACHE_DIR`, `OPENCODE_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCODE_LOG_DIR` variables is exactly what's needed for portable installs, containers, and cases where you just need things in a specific place.

While looking at this I kept thinking about a related but slightly different use case, and wanted to raise it since this PR is already touching the right code: a companion variable called **`OPENCODE_APPNAME`**, similar to how Neovim handles [`NVIM_APPNAME`](https://neovim.io/doc/user/starting.html#%24NVIM_APPNAME).

The idea is simple — instead of overriding individual paths, `OPENCODE_APPNAME` would just substitute the `"opencode"` app name used when building all four XDG paths at once. So `OPENCODE_APPNAME=opencode-work` would naturally produce `~/.local/share/opencode-work`, `~/.cache/opencode-work`, `~/.config/opencode-work`, and `~/.local/state/opencode-work`. One variable, full isolation, no path arithmetic required. You'd just alias `opencode-work` and `opencode-self` and be done with it.

I see these as solving different problems rather than overlapping. The `OPENCODE_*_DIR` variables are for when you know exactly where you want things — DevOps, portable installs, CI. `OPENCODE_APPNAME` is more for "I want a work profile and a personal profile and I don't really care where they live, I just don't want them stepping on each other."

The precedence would be straightforward — explicit path overrides win over the app name derivation:

```
OPENCODE_DATA_DIR  >  OPENCODE_APPNAME  >  XDG default ("opencode")
```

So if you set `OPENCODE_DATA_DIR`, that still wins for data regardless of what `OPENCODE_APPNAME` is. They compose without conflict.

The concrete pain point driving this: separate OAuth logins. Right now `auth.json` has one entry per provider — if you have a work Copilot account and a personal one, re-logging into one overwrites the other. `OPENCODE_APPNAME=opencode-work opencode` would give each identity its own isolated `auth.json` without any user needing to think about XDG paths. There's some related discussion over in #11830 as well.

Not pushing for this to land in this PR necessarily — might be cleaner as a follow-on. But since the path logic is already being touched here it seemed worth flagging.

## Root cause

The rewriting happens **server-side on Anthropic's API**, not in OpenCode. In [`provider.ts` (~line 126)](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts), OpenCode unconditionally sends `anthropic-beta: claude-code-20250219,...` with every Anthropic request. Anthropic's server sees that flag and rewrites `opencode` → `claude`/`Claude` in the entire system prompt — including user-provided AGENTS.md content and `Instructions from:` paths.

There's no string replacement in OpenCode's source. You can verify: `anthropic.txt` says "You are OpenCode" but the model receives "You are Claude Code".

`OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1` doesn't help — it only controls CLAUDE.md/skills file loading, not the server-side rewriting. Switching auth methods doesn't help either; the beta header is sent regardless.

## Workaround

I developed agent instructions that survive the rewriting. Key techniques:

1. **Split the word**: Write `` `open` + `code` `` instead of the joined word — the rewriter won't match it.
2. **Runtime path discovery**: Instruct agents to `ls ~/.config/ | grep -i open` (etc.) instead of hardcoding paths.
3. **Explicit distrust**: Tell the model not to trust any `claude`/`Claude` paths in its system prompt.

Full implementation in my dotfiles: https://github.com/gotgenes/dotfiles — see the "Path Rewriting Warning" sections in [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/gotgenes/dotfiles/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [`private_dot_config/opencode/agents/retrospective.md`](https://github.com/gotgenes/dotfiles/blob/main/private_dot_config/opencode/agents/retrospective.md).

## Suggested fix

A flag to remove `claude-code-20250219` from the beta header (while keeping `interleaved-thinking` and `fine-grained-tool-streaming`) would let users opt out of the rewriting entirely.

## CI Status Note

The two failing checks are both caused by a single flaky Windows Playwright e2e test (`prompt-mention.spec.ts:4:1 — smoke @mention inserts file pill token`) that is **unrelated to this PR's changes** (stream hooks in the plugin system).

**Passing (6/8):** nix-eval, check-standards, check-compliance, typecheck, unit (linux), e2e (linux)
**Failing (2/8):** e2e (windows) — 95 passed, 1 flaky failure; test (linux) — cascading gate failure from the Windows flake

The stream hooks implementation doesn't touch any UI/prompt/mention code. Happy to rebase if needed, but this looks like a pre-existing flaky test.

I think i know why this is happening
1.Failed Snapshots: Every time you interact with the AI, OpenCode tries to snapshot your workspace. If your project is large (or if you accidentally run it in your home directory), these operations can hang.

2.Orphaned Files: When the process hangs or is killed, it leaves those tmp_pack_... files in your .local/share/opencode/.../objects/pack folder.

3.No Auto-Cleanup: The current version of OpenCode (as of early 2026) doesn't have a built-in mechanism to delete these temporary files automatically once they've failed.
